source_snapshot.procedure: Insert a USB key, copy a file to and from it, check transmission speed, and repeat on every USB 3.0 port.
source_snapshot.criteria: Copy succeeds; speed is reasonable from USB definition; all USB 2.0 ports should match USB 3.0 speed, which contradicts the item/procedure; generic evidence/log checks also apply.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL with dedicated mounted media, but writes only host-to-USB, does not measure speed or copy back, assumes `/mnt/usb`, uses insecure SSH and can overwrite an existing file.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: RPUC/CHANGED with HIGH risk; adds dedicated media, port/speed evidence and flags the USB2/USB3 conflict, but its sample still lacks a complete timed bidirectional copy contract.
source_snapshot.procedure_direct_xlsx: "【Before Test】 1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). 1. Plug a USB key and copy a file to/from the key. 2. Check the transmission speed. 3. Repeat step 1~2 on all other USB 3.0 port.
source_snapshot.criteria_direct_xlsx: 【After Test】 1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test. Criteria: 1. File should be copied successfully 2. Speed value should be reasonable from USB definition 3. All USB 2.0 port should match USB 3.0 speed."
source_snapshot.deepseek_direct_xlsx: PARTIAL | -- USB - File transmission USB 3.0 (USB 3.0 file transmission): needs a USB storage device plugged in by a person; once mounted, agent copies a test file and hashes it sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "mountpoint -q /mnt/usb || { echo 'USB not mounted'; exit 1; }; dd if=/dev/urandom of=/tmp/u1 bs=1M count=512 2>/dev/null && cp /tmp/u1 /mnt/usb/x && sync && md5sum /tmp/u1 /mnt/usb/x 2>&1" to verify the transfer; the initial plug is operator.

disposition_reason: The source explicitly says copy to/from, so both directions are coverage requirements. The proposed copy only writes to media and a hash verifies content at rest but not a separately read-back file or read speed. `sync` affects durability and timing, while page and device caches can inflate measurements. Also USB protocol rate is not a storage throughput guarantee. Most importantly, requiring USB2 ports to match USB3 speed contradicts the named USB3 scope and physical bandwidth tiers; engineering must choose the intended population and thresholds before verdict. test_case.test_name: USB - File transmission USB 3.0 — retained controlled review-layer procedure
test_case.purpose: Verify safe bidirectional file transfer, data integrity and acceptable measured throughput on every intended external USB 3.0 port using dedicated test media.
required_package: Authoritative USB 3.0 versus USB 2.0 port population and correction/interpretation of Criteria 3
Physical port labels and controller/root-hub/connector mapping
Dedicated drive model/serial/capacity/partition/filesystem and approved mount/test directory
Approved file size/content, free-space margin, write/read timing method, cache policy and timeout
Expected negotiated USB generation/link speed and separate minimum sustained write/read payload thresholds per port/media
Safe sync/unmount/removal procedure and kernel error/thermal/media abort criteria
test_case.test_command: Map every physical USB 3.0 port to controller/root-hub path; approve a dedicated empty test drive and unique partition/filesystem/mount; record serial/capacity/free space and negotiated USB generation for each insertion; create one approved incompressible file and source hash; time host-to-USB copy plus durable sync, hash the media file, time USB-to-host read-back to a new file and hash it; collect kernel USB/storage errors; safely sync/unmount before moving the same drive to the next port; never overwrite unapproved paths or infer throughput from signaling rate.
test_case.expected_result: 【After Test】 1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test. Criteria: 1. File should be copied successfully 2. Speed value should be reasonable from USB definition 3. All USB 2.0 port should match USB 3.0 speed."

safety_gate: Use only uniquely identified dedicated test media and a newly created approved test directory; refuse an ambiguous device or mount
Verify capacity/free space and resolved device/mount path before every write; never overwrite operator data or a raw device
Keep the media inserted through durable sync and hash completion; safely unmount before removal or port change
Use secure credentials and verified host identity
Do not clear global caches or alter kernel/storage settings unless separately approved; disclose cache effects in results
Stop on disconnect, reset, I/O error, hash mismatch, filesystem warning, abnormal temperature or unexpected kernel event; no automatic retry
expected_evidence: Resolved required-port matrix and physical label/controller/root-hub mapping
Per-port negotiated USB topology/generation and insertion timestamps
Source file identity/size/hash, timed host-to-USB plus sync output and media-file hash
Timed USB-to-host read-back output and read-back hash matched to source
Per-port write/read payload rates versus approved thresholds, kernel USB/storage logs, safe unmount and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: Until engineering resolves Criteria 3, do not silently convert USB2 ports into USB3 expectations or omit any ports. Preserve the Master wording and report the conflict.

source_conflict.reason: Item and Procedure explicitly target every USB 3.0 port, but Criteria 3 explicitly says every USB 2.0 port should match USB 3.0 speed. USB2 signaling cannot normally meet USB3 signaling speed, so the authoritative port scope/expectation cannot be inferred safely.

blocked.reason: A safe review-layer method is defined; missing project values are runtime gates rather than a review blocker.
